item.title: FDOT to resurface SR 89 in Milton; virtual update planned
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Transportation is holding a virtual project update for a major resurfacing effort on State Road 89 (Dogwood Drive) between U.S. 90 and S.R. 87 in Milton. The roughly $20-million project will resurface existing travel lanes, auxiliary lanes, median crossovers, and paved shoulders. Beyond repaving, FDOT plans to upgrade…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Transportation is holding a virtual project update for a major resurfacing effort on State Road 89 (Dogwood Drive) between U.S. 90 and S.R. 87 in Milton.

The roughly $20-million project will resurface existing travel lanes, auxiliary lanes, median crossovers, and paved shoulders. Beyond repaving, FDOT plans to upgrade pedestrian infrastructure to meet Americans with Disabilities Act standards, add buffered bike lanes, and improve traffic signals, signs, pavement markings, drainage, and lighting. No additional land acquisition will be needed.

Construction bids are scheduled for early 2028. Project details—including maps, drawings, and timelines—are available online at https://storymaps.arcgis.com/collections/18effe29792f49d9ae6f41f587c9c0e2. Residents can also contact project manager James Duvall at (850) 415-9021 or jduvall@hntb.com to review materials.

Public comments on the project update are due by Thursday, Dec. 10, 2026.

item.title: Escambia Extension's Lydia Purvis Named November Employee of the Month
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Lydia Purvis, a Horticulture Specialist with Escambia Extension Services, has been recognized as the county's November 2026 Employee of the Month. The Escambia County Board of County Commissioners honored Purvis with a proclamation at its November 5 meeting, citing her strong customer service, positive attitude, and collaborative approach to her…
item.content:encoded:
Lydia Purvis, a Horticulture Specialist with Escambia Extension Services, has been recognized as the county's November 2026 Employee of the Month. The Escambia County Board of County Commissioners honored Purvis with a proclamation at its November 5 meeting, citing her strong customer service, positive attitude, and collaborative approach to her work.

Since joining the Extension office in April 2022, Purvis has managed the Master Gardener Volunteer Program, handled community education about plants and horticulture, and created educational materials and videos for residents. Her role focuses on supporting UF/IFAS Extension's horticulture program while answering public questions about gardening and plant care. Extension Services Director Nick Simmons praised her ability to build relationships across the department and with the public. "She has worked hard to build positive relationships with our clients and staff and brings a can-do attitude to every task she manages," Simmons said in a statement.

Over the past year, Purvis coordinated "Traveling Through Extension," a new community outreach program that brought 135 third-grade students and teachers to the Extension office for educational field trips. The event featured six sessions on topics including animal interactions, food safety, healthy snacks, and plant growth. Purvis secured funding, worked with local schools, and coordinated volunteer efforts to make the program successful.

Purvis, a native of Escambia County, volunteers with several community organizations including Future Farmers of America, 4-H, and her church. She expressed gratitude for the recognition and her Extension team. "Every day in Extension is a new adventure," she said. "My favorite part is helping educate the public about the importance of horticulture."

item.content:encoded:
Curbside recycling service has resumed in Pensacola following disruptions, according to city staff announcements. However, officials are emphasizing the importance of detailed record-keeping as the city pursues Federal Emergency Management Agency reimbursement for disaster-related costs.

The advisory comes as Pensacola works through post-disaster recovery procedures. Staff have flagged that meticulous documentation will be essential to support any FEMA claims related to the interruption and resumption of waste management services.

Residents should continue to follow normal recycling guidelines as service returns to regular schedules.

item.title: FDOT Issues Traffic Alert for I-10, US 90, I-110 Work This Weekend
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Drivers across Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should prepare for significant traffic disruptions over the next week as the Florida Department of Transportation conducts construction and maintenance work on multiple major routes. Starting Sunday, November 8, through Thursday, November 12, nighttime lane closures will affect I-10 in several…
item.content:encoded:
Drivers across Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should prepare for significant traffic disruptions over the next week as the Florida Department of Transportation conducts construction and maintenance work on multiple major routes.

Starting Sunday, November 8, through Thursday, November 12, nighttime lane closures will affect I-10 in several locations between mile markers 11 and 14 (east of U.S. 29 to east of Davis Highway), with work scheduled from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Drivers should expect intermittent lane shifts and periodic ramp closures during those hours. The same timeframe applies to I-110 between I-10 and U.S. 98, where paving operations and roadway construction will create similar disruptions.

US 90 (Scenic Highway) from south of I-10 to south of Hyde Park Road will see lane closures for striping work Sunday through Thursday, 8 p.m. to 5:30 a.m. Law enforcement and traffic flaggers will be stationed at work zones to guide drivers safely through affected areas. SR 292 (Gulf Beach Highway) will also experience nighttime lane closures the week of November 8 for paving, with a 35 mph speed limit in effect and median devices positioned near Patton Drive and Mills Avenue.

Additional ongoing construction includes Garden Street (Business US 98), which remains reduced to two lanes through late 2026, and several I-10 interchanges at Nine Mile Road and U.S. 29 with lane reductions and temporary traffic reconfigurations expected to persist through year's end. FDOT recommends allowing extra travel time and using alternate routes when possible during the work windows.

item.title: Laredo Street to close for sidewalk work in Santa Rosa County next week

Residents will maintain access to their homes during the closure, but drivers should expect delays and plan alternate routes. The…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County will close a section of Laredo Street between Presidio Street and Granada Street beginning Monday, November 9, through Friday, November 13, for sidewalk construction work including ditch regrading.

Residents will maintain access to their homes during the closure, but drivers should expect delays and plan alternate routes. The county recommends using Presidio Street and El Paseo Street to bypass the work zone, depending on direction of travel. Detailed detour maps are available on the county's website.

The Laredo Street Sidewalk Project will ultimately extend sidewalks along Laredo Street from Highway 87 to Ortega Street. The work is funded in part by Area 3 Transportation Impact Fees. The closure timeline is subject to weather conditions.

item.title: FDOT hosting public hearing on 5-year road plan for NW Florida
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Transportation District Three is inviting the public to weigh in on transportation projects planned for 2028 through 2032, including work affecting Escambia and Santa Rosa counties. The hybrid public hearing is scheduled for Thursday, December 10, from 1 p.m. to 2 p.m. CST (2 p.m. to 3 p.m. EST). Residents can participate…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Transportation District Three is inviting the public to weigh in on transportation projects planned for 2028 through 2032, including work affecting Escambia and Santa Rosa counties.

The hybrid public hearing is scheduled for Thursday, December 10, from 1 p.m. to 2 p.m. CST (2 p.m. to 3 p.m. EST). Residents can participate virtually or attend one of three in-person locations: FDOT District Three Headquarters in Chipley, the Milton Operations office in Milton, or the Midway Operations office in Midway. Pre-registration is required for either format and can be completed at the District 3 Tentative Five-Year Work Program Public Hearing registration page.

The tentative work program outlines proposed transportation improvements across 16 NW Florida counties, including roadway, bicycle, pedestrian, freight, trails, transit, aviation, and seaport projects. FDOT will present the plan and collect community feedback during the two-hour hearing. Comments submitted or postmarked by December 20 will be included in the official record. Those needing special accommodations or translation services should contact Carla Hodges, FDOT's District Three Program Management Administrator, at (888) 638-0250, ext. 1213, or carla.hodges@dot.state.fl.us at least seven days before the hearing.

item.title: Rep. Salzman to distribute 30,000 pounds of food at Thanksgiving event Nov. 21
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: State Representative Michelle Salzman and Jennifer Harrison are organizing a drive-through Thanksgiving food distribution on Saturday, November 21st at Marcus Pointe Baptist Church in Pensacola, according to a press release from the representative's office. The event will begin at 7:30 a.m., with vehicles allowed to line up starting at 6:00 a.m.…
item.content:encoded:
State Representative Michelle Salzman and Jennifer Harrison are organizing a drive-through Thanksgiving food distribution on Saturday, November 21st at Marcus Pointe Baptist Church in Pensacola, according to a press release from the representative's office.

The event will begin at 7:30 a.m., with vehicles allowed to line up starting at 6:00 a.m. Organizers expect to serve at least 400 families while supplies last, distributing 30,000 pounds of food total. Each household will receive two boxes: one with a week's worth of groceries and another containing everything needed for a full Thanksgiving dinner. Baby food, diapers, and wipes will also be available in limited quantities.

"This event reflects the power of partnerships and our shared commitment to serving our community during the holidays," Salzman said in the release. "We want to ensure that every family has food on the table and the resources to enjoy a warm Thanksgiving meal together."

The event is being coordinated with Feeding the Gulf Coast and includes support from the Escambia County Sheriff's Office, FPL, HCA Florida West Hospital, State Farm, International Paper, and numerous local businesses and organizations. Those interested in volunteering can contact Jennifer Harrison at 850-324-2744. The church is located at 6205 North W Street, Pensacola.

item.title: ECSO busts 6 in fentanyl operation, seizes nearly 1,000 grams
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Sheriff's Office wrapped up a major narcotics operation this week, announcing the arrest of six individuals and the seizure of nearly 1,000 grams of fentanyl. The crackdown, called Operation Lucky Charms, involved the execution of 28 search warrants across the county. According to WKRG News 5, the operation targeted drug…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Sheriff's Office wrapped up a major narcotics operation this week, announcing the arrest of six individuals and the seizure of nearly 1,000 grams of fentanyl. The crackdown, called Operation Lucky Charms, involved the execution of 28 search warrants across the county.

According to WKRG News 5, the operation targeted drug distribution networks in the area. The scale of the fentanyl seizure underscores the ongoing opioid crisis affecting Escambia County and the broader region.

Details on the specific charges and identities of those arrested were not immediately available. The Sheriff's Office has not yet released information about how the operation was initiated or whether additional arrests are expected.

item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Jesse Guardado, 64, was executed by lethal injection Thursday evening at Florida State Prison for the 2004 murder of a Panhandle woman. According to the Department of Corrections, Guardado was pronounced dead at 6:13 p.m. Guardado had been convicted in connection with the death of a woman who had assisted him after his release from jail. The case…
item.content:encoded:
Jesse Guardado, 64, was executed by lethal injection Thursday evening at Florida State Prison for the 2004 murder of a Panhandle woman. According to the Department of Corrections, Guardado was pronounced dead at 6:13 p.m.

Guardado had been convicted in connection with the death of a woman who had assisted him after his release from jail. The case stems from events in 2004, more than two decades before the execution carried out this week.

The execution marks another completion of Florida's capital punishment cases, which have been carried out at a higher pace in recent years under the state's current administration.

item.content:encoded:
The Community Action Program Committee will set up at Century Town Hall on Friday from 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. to help North Escambia residents struggling with bills and recovery costs.

Eligible applicants can get assistance paying electric, natural gas, and water bills, as well as reconnection fees. The program is also helping people secure temporary housing after recent storm damage.

No appointment is necessary. Residents should bring documentation of income and proof of residency, along with utility bills or other evidence of the expenses they need help covering.

Overnight lows will drop into the low 40s Saturday and Sunday night — a notable shift from earlier in the week. Friday will see increasing clouds during the day with a high near 75 degrees and light north winds at 5…
item.content:encoded:
A pleasant and chilly weekend is setting up for the Pensacola area, with clear skies and lower humidity taking hold through Sunday. Overnight lows will drop into the low 40s Saturday and Sunday night — a notable shift from earlier in the week.

Friday will see increasing clouds during the day with a high near 75 degrees and light north winds at 5 to 10 mph. Friday evening will start out cloudy but clear gradually as the night progresses, with lows bottoming out around 52.

If you're planning outdoor activities over the weekend, conditions should be ideal. Bundle up for early morning and evening hours, particularly Sunday night when temperatures will be at their lowest.

Two North Escambia elementary schools are hosting fall festivals and carnivals today, offering families games, food, and carnival activities.

Byrneville Elementary School, located at 1600 Byrneville Road, will run its annual Fall Festival from 4 to 7 p.m. The event features games, food vendors, a hayride, mechanical bull, haunted house, carnival rides, rock climbing, and an annual basket auction.

Jim Allen Elementary is also hosting its carnival today, though specific times and details for that location were not provided in the available information. Both events offer traditional fall festival fare and are free or low-cost entertainment options for families in the North Escambia area.

item.content:encoded: An Escambia County jury has found Antonio Marshone DeSoto guilty of second-degree murder in connection with the fatal shooting of Charles Black on Main Street in McDavid last February. The jury reached its verdict Thursday afternoon after deliberating for just under two hours. DeSoto, 27, was charged in the death that occurred in the unincorporated North Escambia community. The conviction marks the resolution of a case that has been pending since the 2025 incident.

item.title: Flomaton Police Chief Justin Hetrick Resigns, Mayor Denies Department Closure

The announcement came as Mayor Arthur Odom moved to reassure residents about the department's future. Odom publicly denied…
item.content:encoded: Flomaton Police Chief Justin Hetrick has announced his resignation, submitting his official letter on Monday, Nov. 2, with his final day set for Friday, Nov. 13, according to a Flomaton Police Department Facebook post. The announcement came as Mayor Arthur Odom moved to reassure residents about the department's future. Odom publicly denied circulating rumors that the Flomaton Police Department would close following Hetrick's departure, emphasizing that the agency remains fully operational. Hetrick's resignation comes during a period of apparent concern in the community, though no specific reason for his departure has been made public.

item.title: NAS Pensacola Homecoming Air Show kicks off Friday with free admission
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The 2026 Naval Air Station Pensacola Homecoming Air Show begins Friday and continues through Saturday, offering free general admission to what's traditionally one of the region's largest annual events. The two-day show is expected to draw more than 250,000 spectators to the base. This year's air show, themed "200 Years Forged Here," celebrates NAS…
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Naval Air Station Pensacola Homecoming Air Show begins Friday and continues through Saturday, offering free general admission to what's traditionally one of the region's largest annual events. The two-day show is expected to draw more than 250,000 spectators to the base.

This year's air show, themed "200 Years Forged Here," celebrates NAS Pensacola's bicentennial milestone. The installation has been a cornerstone of naval aviation training and operations since its founding two centuries ago.

The event typically features military aircraft demonstrations, flyovers, and static displays. Attendees should plan for significant traffic and arrive early, particularly on opening day. Parking and shuttle information will be available at the gate.

item.title: Blue Angels ready for homecoming airshow after missing 2025
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Blue Angels are returning to Pensacola this weekend for their season-closing Homecoming Airshow, bringing high-octane flying demonstrations to Naval Air Station Pensacola on Friday and Saturday after last year's event was canceled. Commandeering Officer and Flight Leader Adam Bryan told WKRG News 5 that the homecoming represents a major…
item.content:encoded:
The Blue Angels are returning to Pensacola this weekend for their season-closing Homecoming Airshow, bringing high-octane flying demonstrations to Naval Air Station Pensacola on Friday and Saturday after last year's event was canceled.

Commandeering Officer and Flight Leader Adam Bryan told WKRG News 5 that the homecoming represents a major milestone for the team. "We mark this as our proverbial Super Bowl," Bryan said, underscoring the significance of ending the flying season in front of their home crowd.

The airshow marks the culmination of the Blue Angels' 2026 performance season and gives the precision flying team a chance to reconnect with the Pensacola community that has long supported their operations at NAS Pensacola.

item.title: Blue Angels return to NAS Pensacola for 200th anniversary shows this weekend
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Navy Blue Angels are set to perform at Naval Air Station Pensacola this Friday and Saturday as part of the base's 200th anniversary celebration, according to WKRG-TV 5. The high-speed demonstration team will mark the return of the iconic six-plane formation after a 2025 government shutdown forced the cancellation of previously scheduled…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Navy Blue Angels are set to perform at Naval Air Station Pensacola this Friday and Saturday as part of the base's 200th anniversary celebration, according to WKRG-TV 5. The high-speed demonstration team will mark the return of the iconic six-plane formation after a 2025 government shutdown forced the cancellation of previously scheduled performances.

The flyovers are expected to draw crowds to the Pensacola area as residents and military families gather to witness the precision aerobatic team. The Blue Angels are among the most recognizable symbols of naval aviation and typically draw significant attendance whenever they perform in the region.

This marks a significant milestone for NAS Pensacola, which has been home to naval aviation training and operations for two centuries. The base remains one of the largest employers in the Escambia County area and continues to play a central role in Navy pilot training and fleet operations.

item.title: NAS Pensacola draws 3,000 students for STEAM career event
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Naval Air Station Pensacola hosted its second annual STEAM career education event Thursday, drawing about 3,000 students from across the region. The day-long program introduced attendees to opportunities in science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics, according to WKRG News 5. The event brought together students with military and…
item.content:encoded:
Naval Air Station Pensacola hosted its second annual STEAM career education event Thursday, drawing about 3,000 students from across the region. The day-long program introduced attendees to opportunities in science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics, according to WKRG News 5.

The event brought together students with military and civilian professionals working in STEAM fields, giving young people a chance to explore potential career paths while learning about the diverse roles available within the naval aviation community and beyond. Thursday's gathering represented a significant expansion of what organizers described as their second year hosting the initiative at the base.
